leaders.priorTitle: Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.nextRole: President (16th)
leaders.notes: BGSU's ninth president and first African American president; the sitting leader in 1996, included with his true 1995 start year to anchor the chain. Announced in May 2008 that he was leaving to lead Howard University, where he began August 1, 2008. BGSU trustees granted him the title President Emeritus in May 2017.

leaders.priorTitle: President Emerita (retired 2006 after serving as President 1991-2006)
leaders.nextRole: Retirement; continued higher-education governance work, including co-chair of the Knight Commission on Intercollegiate Athletics
leaders.notes: Came out of retirement as interim president in July 2008 and was named BGSU's tenth president on January 6, 2009, so the entry is recorded as a full presidency rather than interim. She is president emerita of both Kent State and BGSU, an unusual double.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.nextRole: Retirement; stayed on to assist BGSU's comprehensive fundraising campaign and the leadership transition
leaders.notes: BGSU's eleventh president, taking office July 1, 2011. She announced at the December 2017 board meeting that she would step down on December 31, 2017, a year early on a contract running through 2019, and trustees named her President Emeritus at the same meeting.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Senior Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.priorInstitution: Bowling Green State University (internal; provost since 2012, before that dean of the Schmidthorst College of Business 2006-2012)
leaders.notes: Named interim president effective January 1, 2018 and appointed BGSU's twelfth president on February 23, 2018; the first BGSU alumnus to lead the university. Still sitting as of July 2026 with no active presidential search identified.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.nextRole: Retired; named President Emeritus of Cal Poly Pomona (died May 1, 2024, age 88)
leaders.notes: Fourth president; the sitting leader in 1996, included with his true 1991 start year to anchor the chain. Came from CSUN, where he was VP for Academic Affairs 1985-1991. Known for diversity and educational-equity work, founding the cultural centers and iPoly High School.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.nextRole: Retired; named President Emeritus of Cal Poly Pomona
leaders.notes: Fifth president, appointed by the CSU Board of Trustees in 2003 after serving as provost at Fresno State (1999-2003). Announced his retirement January 30, 2014, effective at the end of December 2014; his tenure secured a $42 million Kellogg Foundation gift, then the largest cash gift in CSU history. No interim served between him and Coley, who began January 1, 2015.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.nextRole: Retired; named President Emerita of Cal Poly Pomona
leaders.notes: Sixth president and the first woman and first African American to lead Cal Poly Pomona; appointed September 2014 and took office January 1, 2015 after serving as CSU Bakersfield's provost 2005-2014. Announced February 4, 2025 that she would retire at the end of July 2025. Her tenure drew a nonbinding Academic Senate no-confidence resolution (25-3) on December 6, 2023 over shared-governance concerns.

leaders.priorTitle: Interim Provost and Vice President for Academic Affairs (last active post before her 2022 retirement)
leaders.priorInstitution: California State Polytechnic University, Pomona (internal; she came out of retirement from this same campus)
leaders.nextRole: Concluded her interim term June 30, 2026 and returned to retirement
leaders.notes: Seventh president, serving in an interim capacity from July 28, 2025 to June 30, 2026. A 32-year Cal Poly Pomona veteran: joined the music faculty in 1990, chaired the Music Department, then served as dean of the College of Letters, Arts and Social Sciences and interim provost before retiring in 2022. She is also founder and artistic director of VOX Femina Los Angeles.

leaders.priorTitle: President
leaders.notes: Eighth president and the first Latina to lead Cal Poly Pomona; named by the CSU Board of Trustees in March 2026 following a national search launched after Coley's retirement, and took office July 1, 2026, so she is the sitting president as of July 2026 and there is no active presidential search. She had been the fourth president of CSU Monterey Bay since 2022; earlier provost at Pace University and 21 years at CUNY Hunter College. A neurobiologist by training (PhD, Rutgers).

leaders.priorTitle: President
leaders.nextRole: Retired; President Emeritus
leaders.notes: Took office July 29, 1991 after leading Indiana University of Pennsylvania (president 1985-91). The sitting leader in 1996, included with his true 1991 start year. Longest-serving modern Fresno State president at 22 years; announced retirement in August 2012 and was honored at a June 12, 2013 farewell reception. The John D. Welty Center for Educational Policy and Leadership is named for him.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice Chancellor for Student Academic Affairs and Professor of Family and Community Medicine
leaders.nextRole: Chancellor of the California State University system (2021-2022)
leaders.notes: Named by the CSU Board of Trustees in May 2013 and took office August 1, 2013 as Fresno State's eighth president; first Mexican American and first California native to lead the campus. Left after trustees selected him as system chancellor, a post he began January 4, 2021; he resigned the chancellorship in February 2022 amid criticism of his handling of a sexual harassment complaint during his Fresno State presidency. Died of cancer August 25, 2025 at age 58.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.priorInstitution: California State University, Fresno (internal; provost since July 2019, earlier dean of the College of Arts and Humanities)
leaders.nextRole: Appointed permanent President of the same institution
leaders.notes: Named interim president by Chancellor Timothy P. White in October 2020 and began January 4, 2021, the same day Castro started as CSU chancellor. Served roughly four and a half months in the interim role before the trustees made the appointment permanent.

leaders.priorTitle: Interim President
leaders.priorInstitution: California State University, Fresno (internal; before the interim role, Provost and Vice President for Academic Affairs at Fresno State)
leaders.notes: Appointed Fresno State's ninth president by the CSU Board of Trustees on May 19, 2021, moving up from the interim role. A Fresno State insider: faculty member in Spanish and Portuguese for nearly 15 years, then dean and provost; he immigrated from Mexico at age 10. His tenure has drawn friction, including a September 2024 union petition calling for his resignation and, in 2026, his removal of five longtime Fresno State Foundation board members after a critical Chancellor's Office review. No presidential search is under way; he remains the sitting president as of July 2026.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice President for Academic Affairs and Professor of Mathematics
leaders.nextRole: Retired (died April 18, 2017)
leaders.notes: Became CSUF's fourth president in August 1990; the sitting leader in 1996, included with his true 1990 start year. Longest-serving president in campus history, with enrollment growing from about 25,600 to 36,000. Announced retirement at the fall 2011 convocation and stepped down as interim president Willie Hagan took office January 9, 2012. University Hall was renamed Milton A. Gordon Hall in his honor in 2019.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice President for Administration and Chief Financial Officer
leaders.nextRole: Interim (then permanent) President
leaders.notes: A 16-year CSUF administrator, Hagan was named interim president effective January 9, 2012 and served until June 10, 2012. In an unusual swap, he became interim president of CSU Dominguez Hills effective June 11, 2012, the same day Dominguez Hills president Mildred Garcia started at Fullerton; he was later made CSUDH's permanent president and retired in 2018.

leaders.priorTitle: President
leaders.nextRole: President
leaders.nextRoleInstitution: American Association of State Colleges and Universities (AASCU)
leaders.notes: Appointed by the CSU Board of Trustees on January 25, 2012; her first day at CSUF was June 11, 2012, making her the campus's fifth trustee-appointed president and the first Latina president in the CSU system. Named AASCU president in November 2017 and departed at the end of 2017 (Framroze Virjee took office January 1, 2018). She led AASCU 2018-2023 and then became the 11th Chancellor of the California State University effective October 1, 2023.

leaders.priorTitle: Executive Vice Chancellor, General Counsel and Secretary to the Board of Trustees
leaders.nextRole: President (permanent appointment at the same campus)
leaders.notes: Assumed the CSUF presidency January 1, 2018 under a term/interim appointment made by Chancellor Timothy P. White after Mildred Garcia left for AASCU. He served as CSU's executive vice chancellor and general counsel from January 2014 through December 2017, and before that was a partner for nearly 30 years at the law firm O'Melveny & Myers.

leaders.priorTitle: Interim/term-appointment President
leaders.priorInstitution: California State University, Fullerton (internal; already serving as CSUF's term-appointed president)
leaders.nextRole: President and Chief Executive Officer (from August 19, 2024); CSUF President Emeritus in the interim
leaders.nextRoleInstitution: Association of Governing Boards of Universities and Colleges (AGB)
leaders.notes: The CSU Board of Trustees named him permanent president on March 20, 2019 following a national search, making him the campus's sixth trustee-appointed president. He announced on January 23, 2023 that he would retire effective July 31, 2023 at age 62, and was named president emeritus. AGB named him its next president and CEO, a role he began August 19, 2024.

leaders.priorTitle: Executive Vice Chancellor for Academic and Student Affairs
leaders.notes: Appointed interim president by CSU Interim Chancellor Jolene Koester in April 2023, effective August 1, 2023, to serve until the trustees named a permanent president. She led the campus through the 2023-24 year and the national presidential search, and stepped aside when Ronald S. Rochon took office July 22, 2024. Her post-CSUF role could not be verified from official or press sources.

leaders.priorTitle: President
leaders.notes: Appointed by the CSU Board of Trustees on May 22, 2024 and took office July 22, 2024 as CSUF's 10th president, succeeding interim president Sylvia Alva. He had been president of the University of Southern Indiana since 2018; a first-generation college graduate from Chicago's South Side with a doctorate in educational policy studies from Illinois. Still sitting as of July 2026; the 2024 search that produced him has concluded, so no active presidential search.

leaders.priorTitle: President
leaders.nextRole: President
leaders.notes: Sixth president; the sitting leader in 1996, included with his true June 1994 start year. Came from UNLV, where he was president 1984-1994. Branded the campus 'The Beach' and coined 'Go Beach!' Left in January 2006 to lead Sierra Nevada College, then retired; died in 2025 at age 89.

leaders.priorTitle: President
leaders.nextRole: President
leaders.notes: Seventh president, taking office January 2006 after serving as president of Murray State University (2001-2005). Left CSULB in June 2013 to become president of the LSU System (2013-2019), and later president of Oregon State University (2019-2021).

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Senior Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.priorInstitution: California State University, Long Beach (internal; earlier Dean of the College of the Arts)
leaders.nextRole: Retired
leaders.notes: Named interim president effective July 1, 2013 by CSU Chancellor Timothy White after Alexander's departure for LSU; served through June 2014. He was CSULB's sitting provost before stepping up, and retired after the interim term.

leaders.priorTitle: Dean of the Gevirtz Graduate School of Education
leaders.nextRole: Retired
leaders.notes: First woman to serve as CSULB president; took office July 2014 from her deanship at UCSB's Gevirtz School (where she had also been interim chancellor at UC Riverside 2012-2013). Retired effective June 30, 2025 after roughly 11 years.

leaders.priorTitle: Executive Vice Chancellor and General Counsel
leaders.priorInstitution: The California State University Chancellor's Office
leaders.nextRole: Concluded acting appointment upon the permanent president's arrival
leaders.notes: CSULB alumnus (class of 1982) named acting president effective August 25, 2025, bridging the gap after Conoley's retirement. Came from the CSU Chancellor's Office, where he was executive vice chancellor, general counsel, and secretary to the Board of Trustees. Served until Blanchard took office May 1, 2026.

leaders.priorTitle: President
leaders.notes: Appointed by the CSU Board of Trustees on January 28, 2026; assumed office May 1, 2026 as the sitting president. Came directly from a five-year presidency at the University of Houston-Downtown, and earlier spent six years as CSU Executive Vice Chancellor for Academic and Student Affairs. The national search concluded in January 2026, so no active presidential search.
